title: Java Date
learningObjectives: Use LocalDate to represent a calendar date.
Create dates from the current date and explicit values.
Read date components and format dates.
Add or subtract time with date arithmetic.
Compare dates and calculate periods safely.

understand.concept: Modern Java date and time work is provided by java.time. LocalDate represents a date without a time zone or time of day. Use LocalDate.now for the current date and LocalDate.of for a known date. Date values are immutable: plusDays and minusMonths return new values. DateTimeFormatter formats or parses text, while Period represents a date-based amount of time. Prefer these types over the legacy mutable Date and Calendar APIs for everyday date-only work.
understand.whyItMatters: This topic helps Java developers select and use the right standard-library tools for java date in maintainable applications.
understand.analogy: Think of the collection or date API as a purpose-built tool: its operations communicate the guarantees your program can rely on.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a guide; Java API contracts, equality rules and exception behaviour determine the actual result.

explain.narrative: A LocalDate stores year, month and day and validates calendar rules. It cannot represent an instant or a time zone; use LocalDateTime or ZonedDateTime when those concepts matter. Formatting is explicit with DateTimeFormatter. Pattern letters are case-sensitive: yyyy is year-of-era, MM is month, and dd is day. Date arithmetic handles month lengths and leap years. Comparisons such as isBefore, isAfter and isEqual are clearer than comparing formatted strings.

examples.title: Create a date
examples.code:
import java.time.LocalDate;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { LocalDate exam = LocalDate.of(2026, 12, 5); System.out.println(exam); } }
examples.explanation: LocalDate.of validates and creates a date using year, month and day.

examples.title: Read date parts
examples.code:
import java.time.LocalDate;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { LocalDate d = LocalDate.of(2026, 11, 24); System.out.println(d.getYear()); System.out.println(d.getMonthValue()); System.out.println(d.getDayOfMonth()); } }
examples.explanation: Accessor methods return the date's individual components.

examples.title: Add days
examples.code:
import java.time.LocalDate;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { LocalDate start = LocalDate.of(2026, 1, 30); System.out.println(start.plusDays(3)); } }
examples.explanation: plusDays returns a new date and correctly crosses month boundaries.

examples.title: Format a date
examples.explanation: DateTimeFormatter converts a date to a chosen text representation.

examples.title: Compare dates
examples.code:
import java.time.LocalDate;
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { LocalDate a = LocalDate.of(2026, 5, 1); LocalDate b = LocalDate.of(2026, 5, 10); System.out.println(a.isBefore(b)); System.out.println(b.minusDays(9).isEqual(a)); } }
examples.explanation: Date comparison methods express chronological relationships directly.

questions.prompt: Which java.time type represents a date without a time?
questions.explanation: LocalDate stores year, month and day only.

questions.prompt: How do you create a specific LocalDate?
questions.explanation: LocalDate.of is the standard factory method.

questions.prompt: Which pattern letter represents month in DateTimeFormatter?
questions.explanation: Uppercase M represents month; lowercase m represents minute.

questions.prompt: What is LocalDate unable to represent by itself?
questions.answer: A time of day and time zone
options: A time of day and time zone
questions.explanation: LocalDate deliberately has no time or zone component.
